cards.note: The coverage in Ambanja can be recognized by a person wearing a dark blue T-shirt and black sunglasses.

cards.a: Ambiky - Many palms, brown sandy dirt
cards.note: Ambiky can be recognized by the large number of palms combined with the brown, sandy dirt road. In most of the coverage, there is a person walking in front of the trekker with a grey T-shirt and a brown backpack.

cards.a: Andavadoaka - Greyish hat, red and white shirts
cards.note: The town of Andavadoaka can be recognized by three different people appearing on the coverage; One wearing a greyish hat and a light blue shirt, and two with red and white T-shirts.
Most of the coverage in Antananarivo was taken on the side of a hill looking out over the city, which leads up to the Queen’s Palace, which can be seen near the top of the hill.
Baobab Avenue is easy to recognize by the extremely broad trunked baobab trees along the side of the road.

cards.a: Beach west of Ambiky - Low trees and Low mountains
cards.note: A beach west of Ambiky can be recognized by the low trees combined with low mountains to the northwest.
Belo Sur Mer can be recognized by the large number of palms combined with the blanket of white sand on the ground.

cards.a: Belo sur Mer Beach - Dirty Sand
cards.note: The beach outside Belo Sur Mer can be recognized by the somewhat dirty sand and the curved shoreline with the ocean to the northwest.
Kirindy Mitea National Park can be most easily recognized by having the reddest soil present on Street View in Madagascar.
A piece of coverage, partly taken on a large grassy field, and partly on the side of a sand dune, can be found south of Manahy.

A car with a barely visible grey metal roof rack can be seen by Manahy. There are some locations where the car is completely blurred out, where the shape of the blur is the best indication of the area.
Morondava is most easily recognized by the bald person wearing either a light green or a light red striped shirt. It is also one of few towns where the trekker walks on a paved road.
Morondava has a very smooth sand beach, with the ocean to the northwest. There are a large number of palms visible. A man in a blue shirt can also be a clue for this beach.
A small, very sandy village with the shore to the north can be seen on a small cape north of Andavadoaka. Part of the coverage was taken just outside the shoreline.
A village with the shore to the east can be found north of Andavadoaka.
A second Trekker, going to the northeast of Andavadoaka can be recognized by a person with a light blue T-shirt.

A couple of atolls on the central west coast can be seen on Street View. The northernmost is the smallest, and is easily recognizable as it only consists of sand and you can always see from one shore to the other.

NOTE: Among the five atolls with land coverage, only the two furthest south appear on the map.

cards.a: Nosy Ambariovato - Blue shirt and sunglasses, Light red shirt, Dark red tank top
cards.note:
The coverage on the island of Nosy Ambariovato can be recognized by the people, one wearing a blue T-shirt and sunglasses on their forehead, one with a light red T-shirt and one with a darker red tank top. There is also a fourth person in some of the coverage, wearing a light blue T-shirt. The coverage is very hilly and forested.

There is a village by the northern shore of Nosy Ambariovato.
The trekker next to the RN8 can be recognized by its extreme dryness, combined with the four people wearing red, blue, grey and light blue respectively.

cards.a: Sambirano River  - Red shirt white cap, spotted dress
cards.note: A small section of the coverage by the Sambirano river has two different people present on the coverage; one with a red T-shirt and white cap, and one with a spotted dress.

cards.a: Sambirano River - Blue shirt and sunglasses
cards.note: There are three major sections of coverage along the Sambirano river, most of which can be identified with the single person, wearing a dark blue T-shirt and sunglasses on their forehead. The same person is also present on Nosy Ambariovato.
The coverage on the RN8 between Andriamena and Marofandilia can easily be recognized by the large silver roof rack on the Street View car. The coverage is very dry and sandy.
An area with coverage south of Ambiky can be recognized by the large, solitary green bushes combined with a very slight red tinge in the dirt. Certain parts of the coverage are quite wet.

A blue cart dragged by a black cow on the left and a brown-white cow on the right can be found south of Andavadoaka (First Image).

Another cart dragged by a white cow on the left and a black and white cow on the right can be found just south of Andavadoaka (Second Image).

cards.a: St Augustin - Yellow tank top, blue shirt
cards.note:
Two pieces of coverage can be recognized by two people following the trekker; one with a yellow tank top and one with a blue T-shirt. The first of these two parts is located in the town of St Augustin (First image).

The second part with the same two people is found to the east of St Augustin, going through a hilly landscape with a lot of shrubs (Second Image).

cards.a: Surrounding Andavadoaka - Greyish hat, yellow shirt
cards.note: The main part of the trekker coverage surrounding Andavadoaka can be recognized by either the person wearing a greyish hat and light blue shirt or a person wearing a yellow T-shirt.
Toliara can be recognized as being a generally quite busy-looking town and the only large town on Madagascar with no person following the trekker.
A small settlement is found in the northeastern end of Tsaranoro. The mountains can typically be seen in the background. A rainbow can also be seen in this area.

The Tsaranoro Massif is a large monolithic mountain with trekker coverage. The steep mountainsides, combined with the mountainous area surrounding the coverage makes it very recognizable. The four people following the trekker can also occasionally be a useful clue.
